title: Cap. V open + Obj. 1: election is love unto salvation — therefore from foresight of faith
pass_a_gloss: Chapter V. Certain Arminian objections omitted by the Collocutors are set forth and dissolved. There occur besides in Arminius some other arguments, which are not employed in the Hague Conference; we will also bring these into the midst, and treat them one by one. Very many of that kind are brought forward in the Examination of the Perkinsian Predestination; some elsewhere: which as they offer themselves to us we will discuss. Objection 1. Election is love unto salvation: God cannot love a sinner unto salvation unless he be reconciled to him: But God is not reconciled except to him whom he looks upon as believing in Christ: Therefore God elects no one except from an antecedent intuition of faith.
pass_b_english: Cap. V. Certain Arminian objections the Collocutors left out are set out and answered. Arminius has further arguments not used at the Hague Conference; we bring those in too and treat them one by one — many from his Examination of Perkinsian Predestination, some elsewhere. Obj. 1. Election is love unto salvation. God cannot love a sinner unto salvation unless reconciled to him. But God is reconciled only to one he looks on as believing in Christ. Therefore God elects no one except from an antecedent intuition of faith.
source_text: Cap. V. Objectiones quaedam Arminianae a Collocutoribus omissae ponuntur et dissolvuntur. Alia apud Arminium occurrunt nonnulla alia argumenta, quae in Collatione Hagiensi non adhibentur; nos ea quoque in medium afferemus, et sigillatim pertractabimus. Ejus generis quamplurima afferuntur in Examine Praedestinationis Perkinsianae; nonnulla alibi: quae uti sese nobis offerent discutiemus. Obj. 1. Electio est amor ad salutem: Deus non potest peccatorem amare ad salutem nisi ipsi sit reconciliatus: Non autem reconciliatur Deus nisi ei quem ut credentem in Christum intuetur: Ergo Deus neminem eligit nisi ex antecedaneo fidei intuitu.
